channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: WATCH: Vikings superfan has only missed 2 home games in 25 seasons
item.description: “GMA” is outside U.S. Bank Stadium with Minnesota Vikings “Fan of the Year,” Lindsey Lorenston, as she is surprised with a pair of tickets to Super Bowl LXI.

item.title: Trump says he plans 'tremendous numbers' of pardons in 2nd half of term
item.description: The president also defended his pardons of Jan. 6 rioters.

item.title: COP31 climate summit: Can we electrify the world?
item.description: The UN's annual climate change summit, known as COP31, opens this Monday in Turkey amid deep concern following deadly heatwaves in Europe and deadly floods in Nepal. A "super El Niño" in the Pacific is also expected to drive more extreme weather events. In response, COP31 host Turkey is set to launch a global initiative aiming to electrify a third of the world economy. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

item.title: 'Such an extraordinary story': What we know so far about Nvidia spying claims
item.description: Shares of artificial intelligence leader Nvidia tumbled early Monday after the chip company said it launched an investigation of CEO Jensen Huang following reports he was targeted by Chinese intelligence. The internal probe comes after a media report that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. France 24's Philip Turle takes a look at what we know so far about the allegations.

item.title: Spain's right holds poll lead over Sanchez's Socialists ahead of November 29 snap election
item.description: Spain's ruling Socialists have narrowed the gap but continue to trail the conservative People's Party, who would need to team up with the far-right Vox party to secure a majority of seats in parliament, pollsters say with three weeks to go before the country's general election.

item.title: Nvidia stock falls after company opens probe into CEO
item.description: Nvidia stock fell on Monday morning in the first trading session since the chip giant said it opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang.

item.title: Russian network used social media to blame French riots on immigration, EU report says
item.description: An internal EU assessment has uncovered a Russian network that aimed to exploit ​last month's riots in France by using social media to blame the unrest on uncontrolled immigration. The assessment, seen by Reuters, offers an insight into how external actors have been exploiting France's domestic turmoil for their ⁠own political ends.

item.title: Melanie C: From Sporty Spice to dance DJ with 'Sweat'
item.description: Melanie Chisholm rose to fame in the 1990s with one of the world's biggest girl bands: the Spice Girls. "Melanie C", "Mel C" and "Sporty Spice" were her nicknames. She went on to have a successful solo career with several hits in the 2000s, including "Never Be The Same Again" with the late Lisa Left Eye from TLC. In recent years, she's taken up DJing electronic dance music and recently released her ninth studio album "Sweat". Marjorie Hache caught up with the fitter-than-ever ex-Spice Girl.

item.title: DOJ leadership shakeup continues as Civil Division chief steps down
item.description: The head of the Justice Department's Civil Division, Brett Shumate, has submitted his resignation, becoming the latest DOJ leader to step down following the midterms.

item.title: Shock and grief in Poland after weekend mass shooting
item.description: Poland was in shock after a weekend mass shooting in which a gunman opened fire, killing six people and wounding 15 in the city of Krakow before police shot and wounded him. The shooter died in the hospital on Monday morning, police said.

item.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years, 6 months in prison for rape, sexual assault
item.description: The actor was found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.

item.title: Nvidia CEO probed over alleged China spy: Who exactly is Jensen Huang?
item.description: AI chip behemoth Nvidia was plunged into turmoil Monday, November 9, after its high-profile CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an affair, with reports saying US officials believe the woman was spying for China. But who exactly is Jensen Huang, and why does this case matter so much?

item.title: Civil servant who juggled up to five government jobs guilty of fraud
item.description: A civil servant has been found guilty of nine counts of fraud after using remote working and sick notes to juggle up to five full-time government jobs at the same time.

item.title: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
item.description: New Delhi, home to over 30 million people, regularly ranks among the world's most polluted areas during winter, with pollution worsening in late October and November. (Image credit: Manish Swarup)

item.title: Thames Water agrees funding into next year ahead of looming deadline
item.description: The UK's biggest water company has agreed to a funding deal, allowing it to continue operating until autumn next year ahead of a November deadline.

item.title: Chef Alan Geaam on building his Parisian culinary empire
item.description: In this edition of Entre Nous, we are delighted to welcome Alan Geaam, a Michelin-starred chef who arrived in Paris in 1999 with a one-way ticket and nothing more than a backpack. Now, 27 years on, he's the founder of a multi-million-euro restaurant empire. He tells us about his journey to success and how he honours his Lebanese roots through his cooking.

item.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years, 6 months for rape and sexual assault
item.description: Comedian Russell ​Brand, once one ‌of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters, ⁠was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison on Monday after he was convicted of raping one woman and ‌sexually assaulting three more around two decades ago.

item.title: France brings forward minimum wage increase in bid to quell unrest
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said ​on Monday he was bringing forward a planned 1.6 percent hike in the minimum wage to December from January, as he sought to defuse a cost-of-living crisis that has sparked some of France's worst civil unrest in years. It comes as Lecornu meets labour groups on Monday in a bid to find solutions to the cost-of-living crisis. France 24's Rochelle Ferguson has more.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand sentenced to over 10 years for rape and sexual assault
item.description: Russell Brand, who became a celebrity darling in the early 2000s, was found guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault in a case brought by six women. (Image credit: Elizabeth Cook)

item.title: COP31: Betting on electricity to break the climate deadlock
item.description: From November 9 to 20, the international community is gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for the UN COP31 conference. At a time when the energy crisis linked to the war in the Middle East has forced countries to confront their dependence on fossil fuels, this new round of climate negotiations is starting off with a new goal: to push for a massive shift toward electricity.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo XIV in Argentina
item.description: The pontiff will celebrate his first mass in Buenos Aires on Monday, which is expected to draw more than a million people.

item.title: Saving the Venetian lagoon: A natural buffer against climate change
item.description: The Venetian lagoon is home to "barene" – salt marshes made of vegetation and mud, which play an important role against the effects of climate breakdown. They absorb CO2 and can store it long term in the soil, even more efficiently than land forests. But erosion and rising sea levels are threatening these natural ramparts. Today, scientists and environmental associations are trying to save these unique ecosystems. Our Italy correspondent Natalia Mendoza reports.

item.title: Fire that killed mother, children and family dog 'caused by electrical appliances'
item.description: A mother, her two children, and the family dog were killed after a fire believed to have been caused by electrical appliances engulfed their home on Boxing Day, an inquest heard.

item.title: 'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.

item.title: Iran 'has mistaken perception' of US midterm result, expert says
item.description: A leading commentator on Iran says the country sees the results of the US midterm elections as giving them a golden opportunity for a sweet deal. Paymon Azmoudeh from Forward Global was speaking amid conflicting statements from the key players about whether there will be further US military action in Iran. President Donald Trump says that renewed strikes on Iran are "highly unlikely" if talks progress. However, Iran's foreign minister says the midterms have brought a ⁠pause to mediators' work.

item.title: All eyes on Rubio as Iran, Ukraine set to dominate G7 meeting in Paris
item.description: G7 foreign ministers began two days of talks in Paris on Monday as they grapple with multiple unresolved global crises. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is likely to face questions about whether the Trump administration will shift its positions on the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran in particular following the Democrats sweeping victory in the midterms. France 24’s Clovis Casali has more.

item.title: COP31: A focus on electrification as extreme weather events shake the world
item.description: Most of the world’s countries are gathering this week for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. This United Nations Climate Change Conference opens amid deep concern following extreme weather events such as the deadly floods in Nepal and a supersized El Niño. Experts say that in uncertain times, it is even more important to accelerate global efforts.

item.title: Thick smog shrouds Delhi after Diwali celebrations
item.description: A thick blanket of smog shrouded India’s capital Monday after firecrackers lit up the skies over New Delhi during Diwali celebrations, compounding dangerously high pollution levels and intensifying the seasonal air pollution crisis that grips the city every year.

item.title: Trump admits deportation policy 'might have been too tough'
item.description: President Donald Trump in his first major interview since his party lost control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections said he thinks his administration was too aggressive on deportations and that he thinks he can work with Democrats in the new Congress on some kind of immigration deal. Trump said his deportation policy was part of the reason Republicans lost, telling CBS’s “60 Minutes” in an interview that aired on Sunday: “I think it might be too tough, yeah.” France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.

item.title: James Bulger's killer Jon Venables to stay in prison after parole refused
item.description: Child killer Jon Venables will stay behind bars after the Parole Board found he still poses a risk to children.

item.title: Rubio will discuss Iran, Ukraine, AI and more with G7 allies in France
item.description: Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven industrialized democracies have begun two days of talks in Paris as they struggle with multiple unresolved world crises amid questions how U.S. President Donald Trump will approach foreign policy after his Repu...

item.title: WATCH: Family's gigantic fern named 'Jeff' goes viral on social media
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to a family in Colorado who has an annual tradition of having to move their gigantic fern, named Jeff, back inside for autumn.

item.title: Explosion at steel plant in Turkey kills at least six, officials say
item.description: A major fire broke out following an explosion at an iron and steel plant in Turkey on Monday, killing at least six people, with eight missing, officials said.

item.title: AI, affair and espionage: Why is Nvidia's chief Jensen Huang under scrutiny?
item.description: Nvidia chief and tech titan Jensen Huang was in the spotlight on Monday after acknowledging an affair with a woman US officials say was working for Chinese intelligence, a claim Beijing denied.

item.title: 'A tricky day' ahead for French PM as he meets with unions amid social unrest
item.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss salaries and purchasing power following a wave of social unrest across France in recent weeks. But, says France 24's Rochelle Ferguson, he faces a tricky task if his is to meet unions' wage demands and take steps towards placating widespread public anger.

item.title: French policemen go on trial over 2020 beating of Black music producer
item.description: Three French policemen went on trial on Monday, November 9, over the beating of a Black music producer they say was not wearing a face mask during the Covid pandemic, in a rare police brutality case to go to court. The assault on Michel Zecler, now 47, triggered renewed outrage in France over police violence, which victims and researchers say is systemic.

item.title: WATCH: Cruise ship worker rescued by fisherman in Pacific Ocean
item.description: A crew member aboard a Royal Caribbean cruise ship was rescued by three fishermen after going overboard miles off Newport Beach, California.

item.title: 'Novaya Gazeta', an independent Russian newspaper critical of Putin, closes
item.description: Russian investigative newspaper Novaya ⁠Gazeta was winding ​up its operations on Monday, November 9, and preparing to quit its central Moscow office after holding its ​final editorial meeting, bowing to what it said was a campaign of state pressure that had made it impossible to carry on reporting.

item.title: COP31 opens with leaders under pressure to tackle climate crisis
item.description: The COP31 climate talks kicked off Monday, November 9, with an early fight over money as the UN's chief urged world leaders to "get serious" about tackling the crisis after a year of devastating weather extremes. Antonio Guterres made his plea as thousands of participants descended on a sprawling expo centre in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya for the UN's annual two-week climate conference.

item.title: New James Bond actor expected 'within weeks' as 'unexpected' frontrunners emerge
item.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, November 9: Papers condemn the Kremlin's closure of Russian independent paper Novaya Gazeta on its last day. Also in Russia: leaked numbers suggest that almost half a million Russians have died in the war in Ukraine. Next: NASA is recruiting astronauts who will live and work on the Moon. Finally: who will be the next James Bond?

item.title: Met Office issues fog warning for second day - with wind and rain to follow
item.description: A new warning for dense fog has been issued by the Met Office – with people being told to expect "difficult travelling conditions".

item.title: Why a South Korean city is turning to a U.S. college to outsmart AI?
item.description: Through civic participation and liberal education, South Korean educators hope to "quietly stitch the fabric of our democracy…before it unravels beyond repair." (Image credit: Anthony Kuhn)

item.title: Joe Biden scales back book tour as he reveals cancer treatment progress
item.description: Former US president Joe Biden said he won't be "able to have as many conversations" about his upcoming memoir as he would want to because of his cancer diagnosis.

item.title: Democrats won big on issues like immigration. But ICE still has the money
item.description: Following Tuesday's "blue wave," Democrats have vowed to reign in ICE's power. What could they actually accomplish? (Image credit: Andrew Caballero-Reynolds)

item.title: Democrats won big. Can they lower your grocery bill?
item.description: Affordability concerns were top of mind for voters heading into the midterms, as tariffs and the war in Iran drove up prices, including food costs. Now, Americans are expecting relief from Washington. (Image credit: Bill Clark)

item.title: On wild Cumberland Island, a land swap proposal stirs controversy
item.description: Visitors, ecologists, park rangers and residents all love this wild barrier island off the coast of southern Georgia. But they have different ideas of how to best protect it. (Image credit: Malcolm Jackson for NPR)

item.title: Supreme Court weighs effort to shield federal law enforcement as ICE complaints rise
item.description: The Supreme Court considers the case of a prisoner who suffered brutal injuries, only to be denied medical care behind bars. He wants to sue the prison nurse in a case that could change the law on holding federal officers accountable. (Image credit: J. Scott Applewhite)

item.title: Congress is coming back to Washington. Here's what to expect
item.description: Lawmakers are coming back to Washington this week after the midterm elections. Republicans plan to finish work on several outstanding issues before Democrats take control of Congress in January. (Image credit: Zayrha Rodriguez)

item.title: U.N. climate talks begin today. Here are 3 things to know
item.description: Countries are gathering in Antalya, Turkey, for the annual U.N. climate conference. Many are frustrated with the lack of focus on fossil fuels, the main driver of climate change. (Image credit: Burak Kara)

item.description: At least 14 people have died after a boat carrying migrants was found near Crete, Greek authorities have said.

item.description: Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to become the next speaker of the House, was interviewed on "This Week" following Democrats' historic victories in Tuesday's election.

item.description: Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms joins "This Week" to discuss Democrats' sweeping victories, and her historic win in formerly red Georgia.

item.title: Seven dead and 114 injured in train crash near Cairo
item.description: At least seven people have died and more than 100 have been left injured in a major train crash south of Cairo, according to the Egyptian Chief Prosecutor’s office.

item.description: The election could have marked a turning point for Native American women.

item.description: One person has died after being hit by a Ukrainian drone attack in western Russia, while Moscow has struck emergency workers on rescue missions.

item.description: Donald Trump has said he was "only kidding" about UFC boss Dana White becoming White House press secretary.

item.title: Finland's navy chief says Russia's presence in the Baltic Sea may have peaked for now
item.description: Russia may have reached the limit of its "peacetime" ability to project force in the Baltic Sea, with the maritime situation "tense" but "stable", the head of Finland's navy has said.

item.title: WATCH: Firefighters give kids a superhero surprise
item.description: Corpus Christi firefighters dressed as superheroes surprised patients at Driscoll Children's Hospital by rappelling down the glass building as kids waved.

item.description: The showing across the country that flipped Congress to Democratic control on Election Day also trickled down to the state and local level.

item.description: Judy and Jan Johnson spoke with ABC News Live about how proud they are to see their grandson, Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, be elected to Senate.

item.description: The suspect, Ronny Guanipa-Chrinos, allegedly made threats to kill President Donald Trump, according to DHS.

item.description: Eddie, a 3-year-old Labrador retriever, was honored for changing the life of his legally blind owner, Luis Rodriguez, through his work as a guide dog.

item.description: Experts describe the computer hardware theft as a sophisticated cargo heist.

item.description: A gunman suspected of killing six people including a British national in Poland on Saturday has died in hospital.
